s1.syndrome_frame: Asymptomatic hypopigmented macules on the face and neck with a 2-year history
salient_findings: Round, hypopigmented macules symmetrically distributed on face and neck
Absence of hair growth in affected areas
Lesions ranged from 2-3 mm to 25 mm in diameter
key_facts: Male patient in his 40s
2-year history of multiple asymptomatic lesions
Lesions are round, hypopigmented macules
Symmetric distribution on face and neck
No hair growth at the site of the lesions
Previous treatment for tinea versicolor was unsuccessful
Histopathologic findings showed plate-like subepidermal tumor
Neoplastic cords consisted of clear/pale epithelial cells
Glycogen accumulation in cytoplasm
Fibrous connective tissue in stroma
Marked elastosis observed in dermis surrounding tumor

shortlist.label: Idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the description of asymptomatic, hypopigmented macules on the face and neck

shortlist.label: Nevus depigmentosus
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with the presence of hypopigmented macules, although typically present at birth or early childhood

shortlist.label: Pityriasis alba
shortlist.why_kept: Presents with hypopigmented patches, often on the face, but usually accompanied by mild scaling and itching

shortlist.label: Vitiligo
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by hypopigmented macules, but often with a more rapid onset and potential for widespread involvement

shortlist.label: Post-inflammatory hypopigmentation
shortlist.why_kept: Could be considered given the patient's history of previous treatment for tinea versicolor, although the lack of inflammation in the case description makes it less likely

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of multiple, round, hypopigmented macules that are symmetrically distributed on the face and neck, along with the absence of hair growth in the affected areas and the specific histopathologic findings, aligns with the characteristics of idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis.

rejected.label: Nevus depigmentosus
rejected.why: Typically presents as a single, well-defined, hypopigmented patch, which does not match the multiple lesions described in the case.

rejected.label: Pityriasis alba
rejected.why: Usually associated with mild scaling and erythema, and often seen in children, which does not fit the patient's age and symptom description.

rejected.label: Vitiligo
rejected.why: Characterized by complete loss of melanocytes leading to depigmentation, often with a more irregular distribution and potentially associated with other autoimmune diseases, which is not indicated in the case.

rejected.label: Post-inflammatory hypopigmentation
rejected.why: Would typically follow an inflammatory skin condition, which is not mentioned in the patient's history, and the histopathologic findings do not support this diagnosis.
